summary_paragraph: A man with advanced HIV/AIDS and a history of toxoplasmosis was admitted with fever, increased tracheal secretions, and respiratory distress. He was found to have healthcare-associated pneumonia caused by MRSA and Pseudomonas, treated with vancomycin and cefepime, and severe C. difficile colitis managed with oral vancomycin and IV metronidazole. During admission, he was noted to have right-sided weakness and hip pain, leading to imaging that revealed a right intertrochanteric femur fracture, which was surgically repaired with ORIF. His neurological symptoms were attributed to toxic encephalopathy with improvement in cerebral toxoplasmosis on MRI, and he was maintained on antiseizure medication. He experienced episodes of SVT, managed with adenosine and started on metoprolol. His respiratory status improved, allowing weaning from mechanical ventilation to trach mask support. Hypernatremia resolved with free water flushes. He was discharged to extended care with plans for physical therapy, orthopedic follow-up, and continued HIV management.
